text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Vifor Ionita, President of the National Oil Company (CRP), is quoted as saying that hidden subsidies over the past years had seriously affected Romania's oil sector.
- The managers of the Petrotel SA and Vega SA refineries have started legal procedures to close down their loss-making plants, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Tractorul SA tractor maker in the Transylvanian city of Brasov will cut 1,000 jobs over the next three months.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The prices of edible oil and sugar are expected to rise following higher costs for farming works.
- Romanian and foreign investors are willing to buy the refineries earmarked for closure, the paper said.
- The inclusion of the Romvag SA rolling stock maker on the list of 17 loss-making companies slated for closure has been a mistake, the paper quotes an Industry Ministry official as saying.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Freight traffic in the Black Sea port of Constanta is on the decline, the paper said.
- The government will rule on the structure of the new national oil company this week.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Bucharest has scores of right-wing gangs who fight against Gypsies and promote violence, the paper said.
- Investors in the troubled FMOA mutual Fund threatened to stage protests outside the Cotroceni presidential palace in a bid to retrieve their deposits.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Hundreds of buildings in Bucharest might collapse if an earthquake hits the capital city, the paper said.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
